entry.title: Hans Dieter Beck (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Hans Dieter Beck (pictured), a co-head of the publisher C. H. Beck, rode a bicycle to work until he was 92?

entry.title: 2023 Aston by-election (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the 2023 Aston by-election was the first time in more than 100 years that the governing party won a seat from the opposition at an Australian by-election?

entry.title: Walter III Brisebarre (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Walter III Brisebarre renounced the lordship of Beirut to inherit a greater lordship from his father-in-law, only to permanently lose both upon the deaths of his wife, Helena of Milly, and their daughter Beatrice?

entry.title: Born in the U.S.A. (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Born in the U.S.A. was the first compact disc to be manufactured in the United States for commercial release?

entry.title: Ívar Bárðarson (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Ívar Bárðarson's 14th-century reports of feral livestock inhabiting a failed Greenlandic colony were corroborated by the discovery of a frozen goat and animal feces inside an abandoned home?

entry.title: Princess Mononoke (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Princess Mononoke was the most expensively animated, most expensively promoted, and highest-grossing Japanese film of its time?

entry.title: Raging Bull (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Raging Bull was the first hypercoaster to feature a twister layout?

entry.title: Albis Tunnel (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the Albis Tunnel was the second-longest railway tunnel in Switzerland when it was built?

entry.title: Morph (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Morph was included in X-Men: The Animated Series because the writers "really wanted to kill somebody"?
